verdicts.proposedText: Not modeled: the field's continuous Anemo application (self-swirl) to the active character standing inside it.
verdicts.rationale: The heals are fully modeled, but the field's continuous Anemo imbue on the active character — the self-swirl that drives cleansing and swirl planning during the field — is silently omitted (no infusion-of-recipient primitive for summon fields). The kit text explicitly promises this behavior, so a player planning cleanse/swirl timing around the field is misled by a timeline that shows only heal ticks. This is a real CANNOT-model gap, not a constitution exclusion.

groundedIn.claim: The field continuously applies Anemo to characters inside it
groundedIn.quote: Continuously regenerates HP of characters within the AoE and continuously imbues them with Anemo.

groundedIn.claim: The imbue targets the active character, is the self-swirl mechanic, and is not modeled
groundedIn.quote: Field also continuously imbues the active character with Anemo (self-swirl mechanic in gcsim — see burst.go ReactWithSelf, ticks alongside each heal tick); not modeled — no infusion-of-recipient primitive for summon fields.

verdicts.proposedText: Shown on every Normal Attack hit; in game each hit has only a 50% chance to heal, so the timeline shows about double the real healing frequency.
verdicts.rationale: The heal effect is authored on onHit for Normal Attacks with no probability gate, so the timeline visibly fires the team heal on every N hit while in-game it procs 50% of the time — a doubled, on-screen heal frequency. This is a visible divergence affecting heal expectations, squarely inside the purpose test. The effect fires automatically (onHit), so manual-trigger phrasing does not apply.

groundedIn.claim: Each Normal Attack hit has a 50% chance to heal in game
groundedIn.quote: On hit, Jean's Normal Attacks have a 50% chance to regenerate HP equal to 15% of Jean's ATK for all party members.

groundedIn.claim: The timeline shows the heal on every Normal hit, doubling the real frequency
groundedIn.quote: The 50% proc chance is not modeled in the current effect schema — the heal renders on every Jean N hit, doubling its actual frequency.

verdicts.rationale: C1 is a damage-magnitude bonus (+40% DMG on the held skill cast) plus a pull-speed increase. The timeline never displays damage numbers or magnitudes (out of scope by constitution), the bonus creates no buff window, duration, or timing consequence a timeline could omit, and pull speed is crowd-control flavor no user expects a timeline to model. Additionally, hold duration is not a distinct input for this skill (input is just E), so there is nothing on screen that diverges. Nothing here would mislead a player reading the timeline.

groundedIn.claim: C1 is a pull-speed increase plus a 40% DMG increase gated on holding more than 1s
groundedIn.quote: Increases the pulling speed of Gale Blade after holding for more than 1s, and increases the DMG dealt by 40%.

groundedIn.claim: The effect is unauthored and conditional on hold duration
groundedIn.quote: Effect not yet authored — C1 grants +40% DMG to Gale Blade when held for ≥1s (≥60 frames). Conditional on hold duration; not modeled in gcsim skill frame data. Reviewer to author.

verdicts.rationale: C2 triggers on Elemental Orb/Particle pickup, which is out of scope by constitution (pickup-driven empowerment / particle collection), and its payload is Movement SPD + ATK SPD — attack-speed is likewise constitutionally out of scope and movement speed is something no user expects a timeline to model. The curators intentionally stubbed it under the stub-with-caveat philosophy for exactly this reason, noting it auto-fulfills in canonical rotations anyway. Doubly excluded; no caveat warranted.

groundedIn.quote: When Jean picks up an Elemental Orb/Particle, all party members have their Movement SPD and ATK SPD increased by 15% for 15s.

groundedIn.claim: Particle/orb pickup is out of scope by the tool constitution and auto-fulfills in canonical rotations
groundedIn.quote: particle/orb pickup is out-of-scope per the tool constitution; auto-fulfills in canonical rotations
